newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico needs $24.5 bln for infrastructure - Concamin.
newsitem.headline: Mexico needs $24.5 bln for infrastructure - Concamin.

text.p: In the next five years Mexico will require some $24.5 billion of investment in infrastructure, according to a study published by the Conferderation of Industrial Chambers (Concamin).
The confederation said in its monthly publication Industria that roads require the most investment, $12.25 billion, followed by electricity projects, $3.6 billion.
"One of the current national priorities to be considered for any development plan is infrastructure to the extent that it affects all other actions in industrial activity," the study said.
The confederation said natural gas is in need of $2.45 billion, railroads $1.85 billion and airports $1.65 billion. The government is planning privatizations in all three of those sectors.
The petrochemical unit that the government seeks to privatize requires $1.6 billion, the study said.
